"Melee weapon" is Just Another Keyword in VTES. Like "Vehicle" or "Haven".
There's no specific definition to it, just a guideline to what tends to
constitute them at design time.

This guideline is broken in a few cases: Gas powered chainsaw (not strength
based), Rowan ring (doesn't even do damage), and Kerrie (has a ranged
component, which makes it a Ranged Weapon for the purposes of cards that
see it that way). No big deal.

Messages.Author: Dasein
Messages.Body:
> Shenanigans. This is the most assanine thing I have ever heard. I will
> not sell my cards immediately in the hope that good sense will prevail
> and a reverse ruling made.

There are a bunch of weird things in the game that don't make sense.
Like a repo man being able to find you a helicopter ("look what I found
in the yard out back! Damn yuppies, they can never keep up the payments
on their choppers").

I think the biggest one is Memories of Mortality, the card I generally
refer to as "I was a teenage War Ghoul" (they seem to have left out the
"Mortal" keyword from the card text).

"Oh no, here comes the War Ghoul! ( / renegade garou / succubus / etc
etc). "Damn I remember when I was a giant blob of malformed corpses
stuck together with Tzimisce magic... all the kids at school picked on
me... none of the girls would go to the prom with me... I know his
pain! How could I harm such a beautiful creature with which I share
such a natural affinity..."
Ridiculous stuff really. There are a bunch of other examples you can
easily think of (Ambrosius the ferryman goes computer hacking, a
vampire with a sports bike blocking a vampire flying around in a
Learjet, etc.)
But basically, the cards should really only be thought of as cards;
e.g. a Learjet is a "card that lets you draw cards", not a big plane.
If it WAS a plane and functioned in the game how planes do in real
life, it would obviously be extremely difficult if not impossible to
block a vampire using it. Trying to translate all the cards to
real-world situations just doesn't always work, unfortunately.

So rather than continually errata all the cards and make lots of
exceptional rulings, White Wolf just tells us to deal with it. Which
while at times feels frustrating, is actually a lot easier than having
multiple versions of cards flying around and having to check for the
latest rulings on cards all the time (e.g. Anachronism only works on
certain weapon types considered to be "modern weapons", the following
cards are retrospectively considered to have the card text "modern",
the following are not, blah blah blah).

See the recent debate about whether or not sports bikes are considered
to be "electronic" equipment. The less of that malarkey we have to put
up with, the better.

of the game.

While I agree that endless card clarifications/errata are not a good
thing for the game, I also think we should consider design intent.
Anachronism came out with Ancient Hearts, and let's face it, WotC
weren't ones to really be far sighted. It's clear by the intent of the
card that it should affect only modern day weapons, and since the only
archaic ranged weapon at the time was Ivory Bow, it was explicitly
exempted. (Why they never thought that another archaic ranged weapon
could be created is beyond me. It had me wondering when I first got the
card all those years ago). It just seems bad form to me that one card
is exempt by virtue of it being in existence at the time, while any
other cards that would have been included in the exemption as well
aren't covered simply because of poor card text. Unless there is
something extremely special about the Ivory Bow that I fail to realize?

Of course, this all pretty academic, and fairly cornercase, I've only
seen Anachronism once in the past 3 years. It was reprinted in the 10th
anniversary set, without modification, and it would seem unlikely to
see print again, and thus receive any sort of 'fix'.

And while I haven't followed the Electronic debate, I can understand
the confusion and questions about it. If a new term is brought into the
game, then it should be applied universally to the game. If
'Electronic' isn't to become a trait, then why use the term in the
first place, or use e.g. in brackets, which suggests there are others?
Just list the pieces of equipment and be done with it, like
Anarchronism, and let any other pieces of future electronic equipment
be exempt from Smite. The only thing I can see is that it gives WW the
option to introduce Electronic as a trait later on, but why not do it
now rather than then, which would just mean potentially more cards need
to be so clarified?

The one problem with new cards and expansions is that eventually new
ideas come up that require modifications to existing cards, or that the
new idea is never brought to fruition. Should a card such as Resticted
Airspace, which prevents the use of flying vehicles, just never be
considered, because it would require adding the Flying trait to a few
vehicles? I do understand the difficulties with implementing new
concepts and traits, as not everyone has access to the latest card
text, and thus confusion can certainly arise. But then, this will
happen any time there is an errata or text migration, and then really,
does it matter if one or twenty cards are modified at the same time?

Personally, I would like to see such changes, to give a better 'feel'
to the game, rather than just having card text. Otherwise, why bother
with names and pictures to give a sense of reality to it? I doubt I'd
have played the game if all the cards were simply things like Obfuscate
1 - +1 stealth/+2 stealth, Obfuscate 2 - +1 stealth/block fails,
Obfuscate 3 - +2 steath on non-bleed actions/+3 stealth on non-bleed
actions, etc. It's the image of what is happening, of the minions using
their abilities to do all these things, that make the game so enjoyable
to play.

Just my thoughts,
Chris, Thrall of Arika

Right. But it's not always possible that they make sense; sometimes
they don't make sense at all (like the example someone had of a leather
jacket protecting against a white phosphorus grenade; they also stop
RPG rounds, which is even more ridiculous).

> There are some people who are only interested in the rule aspect of the

Don't get me wrong, I do too.

> One of the beauties of VTES for me is that a combat in VTES

> dont tell us, that we should have no interest in the simulation aspect of the game.

Ok maybe I wasn't clear enough. I'm not telling anyone to have no
interest in the simulation aspect of the game. I'm telling people that
we have to play by the rules, even if they don't make sense in the
'real world' (or the 'World of Darkness world', or any other world you
care to think of). If your vampire fires an RPG at a Loyal Street Gang,
then they survive (must be a very big jacket also to protect a whole
gang of homeboys). It makes no sense at all, in anyone's world, no
matter how you imagine it, but for the purposes of the game, it's just
what happens, because that's what the cards and the rules say. And
White Wolf's general policy is to stick to what the cards and rules
say, even where it doesn't make sense, and even where there seems to be
some original intention for them to work another way (e.g. I think
Memories of Mortality was originally intended to only work on mortal
allies; I think Anachronism was intended to stop vampires using
handguns, rifles, assault rifles, rocket launchers, etc.)

Rather than continually change the cards and the rules, they tell us
that "it's just how it works". And my point is that, while that means
some things make no sense if you think about it in a game world
situation, it's just how the cards are. And that policy makes the game
a lot easier to learn and play, since cards don't change often.
Memories of Mortality just stops a vampire from blocking allies, full
stop. Like I said, if you think about it just as a card, then you're
fine. It's a card that stops you blocking allies. Switch off your World
of Darkness goggles for a moment when somebody plays that card and it's
all good. Yes it would be cool if all the cards made sense in a World
of Darkness way, but that's just the way it works.

>
> Frank

That would still be a "ranged weapon", because ranged weapon has been
defined as a weapon that does damage at range.

"Melee weapon", as a keyword in V:TES, has absolutely zero meaning. It
just applies when other cards make use of it, such as Undead Strength
being usable on a strike with a melee weapon. It doesn't have any
meaning beyond that, just like "Black Hand" or "Gun" has zero meaning in
the game beyond what card text gives it. It's just a word with no
rules-specific meaning.

Messages.Author: Thrall of Arika
Messages.Body:


An unfortunate truth. Make no mistake, I think WW does an excellent job
in attempting to convert abilities and concepts into a card game. Some
things are just very difficult to simulate effectively, or attempts to
make a card act as it would in a 'real' sense just make the card
wallpaper. I think the intent of Memories of Mortality was to be more
along the lines of mortals, and those that appear that way (mages, for
example, or even zombies ... zombies are people too! Well ... were
...). But it seems that with the expansions, we sort of moved away from
mortal allies to other interesting types ... werewolves, demons, etc. I
certainly don't advocate making Memories mortal only (though I doubt it
would hurt the card too much, with the Imbued), but it does stretch the
limits of card flavour and game mechanics.

I have recently been taking notes of games we've been playing, and
attempting to write an actual story based around what happens (which
reminds me, I still have to write up the one for the last tournament we
had). I'll probably do the same for the prerelease too. It certainly
takes some doing to think of how to conceptualize some aspects of what
happens. But I also find that it makes it easier to see how things
work, even if they don't make sense right away. Such as the Gang with
Leather Jacket vs. the RPG Launcher. It's not too hard to consider that
each of the gang members gets a jacket (bulk purchase discount!), that
the rocket doesn't actually hit them, but explodes nearby while they
duck and cover, their jackets getting shredded and singed as a result,
but leaving them alive and breathing.

Have to admit though that it's harder to explain a Laibon with an
Elephant Guardian blocking someone's attempt to steal from Powerbase:
Washington DC, say ... You'd think someone would notice the elephant
circling around the Washington Monument ... And still can't rationalize
the Hell Hound on a Sports Bike either ...

But I think I speak for a lot of people that a lot of the interest in
the game is in the imagery, not just the actual game mechanics (which
are good and solid, of course). Without the vampire background, though,
how much interest would there be in the game? It is much more
interesting and fun to play with Memories of Mortality, rather than
Can't Block or Hurt Allies.

I still advocate card intent/concept over game mechanics though, as in
the case of Anarchonism. It just seems strange that it will affect a
weapon that is probably one of the oldest around (I don't know, but I'm
presuming that the Kerrie is a ceremonial type club/staff), and yet not
the relatively newer weapon in the Ivory Bow. Still, relatively moot,
except in certain environments, and so doubtful that such a change
would ever come about.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

"Bushmen" (for the San) and "Hottentot" (for the Khoikhoi), or
collectively the Khoisan, are not identified (or used) as derogative
terms outside of South Africa. Now, White Wolf would probably be happy
to be informed of the international usages of the words as described in
the "Oxford Dictionary of South African English". If they then see fit
to go into detail about how 'kerrie' is perfectly correct, they can use
"Khoisan", giving up some recognizability outside of South Africa in
exchange.

That they call it a knobkerrie does not preclude them from also calling
it simply a kerrie. "knob" part comes from the Dutch "knop" (knob) and
the kerrie comes from the Nama (a Khoisan language) word variously
tranliterated "kerrie" "kieri" or "kirri" (stick). So even if they
sometimes call their sticks "knobsticks", they're still sticks. (I
assume it's Nama, anyway.)
